sd_veiny.blurb: Veiny is a small, fairly detached formation in the Needles of Rushmore, set apart from the larger cluster of rocks around the Chopping Block. It holds about two dozen lines, mostly bolted sport routes, with a handful of trad lines and a few easy boulder problems. Most of the rope climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.10, and the 5.10 grade is the most common, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on moderate face climbing and want a quieter spot than the busier walls nearby. Expect short routes and a walk past a couple of neighboring formations to reach the base.

sd_big_gash_the.blurb: The Big Gash is a narrow granite slot that splits Turtle Rock on Iron Mountain, near Keystone in the Black Hills. The walls are smooth and sculpted by wind, with vertical to slightly overhanging sport lines and a few crack climbs for trad. Roughly two dozen routes are here, and nothing is easier than 5.9; the bulk sit at 5.11, with a good number of 5.9 and 5.10 lines and a half-dozen at 5.12, which earns it the nickname 5.11 Alley. The slot stays cool in the afternoon, can funnel wind, and most routes want a 60 m rope.

sd_wars_wall.blurb: Wars Wall is a limestone sport wall at the right-hand end of the Mohican sector of Spearfish Canyon in the northern Black Hills. The face is streaked and slightly overhanging, covered in pockets, slots and jugs. It has over twenty bolted routes and is a place for strong climbers: the great majority are 5.12, with a handful of 5.11 and only a couple of easier or harder outliers. Routes are about one rope length. Routes start off a separate block fitted with a couple of belay bolts, and the wall is reached by a short trail along the creek from the canyon road.

sd_outer_outlet.blurb: Outer Outlet is a freestanding granite spire in the Needles of Custer State Park, a hike from Sylvan Lake and farther out than its twin, Inner Outlet. It is steep on every side with no walk-up route, so summits mean multi-pitch climbing and rappelling. About two dozen routes are mostly trad, with a few bolted lines, spread from 5.7 up to the low 5.14 range. The bulk are 5.10 to 5.12, many of them thin, bold face climbs with widely spaced bolts, plus crack lines such as a long fist crack on the south side. Bring a rack and two ropes for the descent.

sd_white_house_wall.blurb: White House Wall is the main face of the Emancipation formation in the Needles behind Mount Rushmore, facing mostly west with a few lines wrapping toward the north. All of its roughly two dozen routes are trad, from an easy 5.6 up to the low 5.13 range, with most between 5.9 and 5.12. Many are long multi-pitch lines, so it works well for climbers who want a full day on granite and less company than the best-known three-pitch route attracts. The walk up from the roadside pullout follows a vague trail over big boulders, and the descent is by rappel.

sd_oltons_shoulder.blurb: Oltons Shoulder is the highest formation on the west side of Highway 244 near Mount Rushmore, in the Needles area of the Black Hills. Most of what is here is bouldering, around twenty problems scattered through a roadside drainage and up the slope, with a few trad and sport lines on the formation itself. Boulder grades run from very easy to hard, with the heaviest cluster at V3 and V4. It gets less traffic than other Rushmore zones, tends to be breezy, and most blocks pick up good sun. A short uphill walk on a faint path leads in from the pullout.
